long_biography.plain_text:
Before Gerald A. “Gerry” Buchheit Jr. became prominent as a Western New York developer, his work was tied to the practical technology of highway marking. A road-surface abrasion system filed in his name in 1990 was assigned to Accent Stripe. He later became chief executive of the Orchard Park family company, whose crews stripe roads and remove existing markings.

Property became Buchheit's second durable operating field. He was managing Quaker Crossing by 1998 and later appeared as its owner, overseeing the Orchard Park retail center through tenant changes, traffic planning and additional construction. He also sponsored Queen City Landing on Buffalo's Outer Harbor, proposing a mixed-use waterfront building with apartments, shops, restaurants and public access.
